rfi.description: Police arrested 1,314 people and 53 officers were injured during Saturday’s protests across France, the interior ministry said on Sunday, as authorities defended a reinforced security operation aimed at keeping marches safe and protecting shops.

rfi.title: France and Britain test NATO readiness with major airborne exercise in Germany
rfi.description: French paratroopers have joined British forces in a major military exercise in Germany, testing their ability to deploy together to defend Nato territory against an enemy equipped with drones and electronic warfare capabilities.

rfi.title: 'The major risk remains a human-directed attack', cyber threat expert warns RFI
rfi.description: Artificial intelligence is changing the pace of cybercrime, helping attackers hunt for security weaknesses, break into computer systems and steal valuable information. For the specialists trying to stop them, the challenge is to keep up. Cyber threat expert François Deruty told RFI this means finding ways to turn the same technology to their advantage.

rfi.title: ‘We want to stop being afraid’: thousands join anti-RN demonstration in Orléans
rfi.description: Thousands of people marched peacefully through Orléans on Saturday to protest against the far-right National Rally as the party held its congress a few kilometres away, with demonstrators calling for solidarity and voicing their concerns about 2027.

rfi.title: Paris march ends in clashes after largely peaceful protests across France
rfi.description: Clashes broke out at the end of a Paris protest on Saturday after a largely peaceful march that drew 110,000 people, according to police, as fresh demonstrations took place across France.

rfi.title: Young Israeli voters lean right, as election puts Netanyahu to the test
rfi.description: Young Israelis preparing to vote in parliamentary elections on Tuesday are leaning further to the right than their elders, with some drawn to the far right and its focus on security. In Rehovot, a city whose results tend to mirror the national vote, RFI met a generation shaped by the attacks of 7 October, 2023 and three years of war.

rfi.title: Azerbaijan hijab ban exposes strain in ‘brotherly’ ties with Turkey
rfi.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, a staunch advocate of Muslim rights, has been notably silent on Azerbaijan’s recent hijab ban in schools. For years, Erdogan and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev have shared a close alliance, but the ban is putting the Turkish president in a tight spot.

rfi.title: In Germany’s Halligen islands, a bird sanctuary faces rising sea levels
rfi.description: Three out of five bird species are in decline worldwide, and one in eight is threatened with extinction. In the Halligen islands of northern Germany, a sanctuary for migratory birds is under threat due to rising sea levels. These 10 small islands – listed as a Unesco World Natural Heritage Site – are home to hundreds of thousands of migratory birds travelling between Africa and the Arctic Circle, as well as many breeding birds.

rfi.title: Deadly shooting west of Paris ‘clearly terrorist’ attack, interior minister says
rfi.description: One person was killed and four others were wounded, including a 12-year-old girl, when shots were fired from a car in two suburbs west of Paris on Friday. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the shooting was “clearly a terrorist crime” and “a racist, probably Islamophobic attack”.

rfi.title: France mobilises 70,000 police and gendarmes for Saturday protests
rfi.description: France will deploy some 70,000 police officers and gendarmes nationwide during a fresh round of protests this weekend, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said on Friday, as President Emmanuel Macron met with student organisations at the Élysée Palace for the first time since the high school protests started more than a month ago.

rfi.title: ‘Too arrogant, too sure of itself’ France confronts its legacy in Africa
rfi.description: Fifteen years after France promised a new relationship with Africa, Paris is still struggling to reconcile its rejection of colonial-era interference with its desire to retain influence on the continent. RFI Africa specialist Christophe Boisbouvier argues in a new book that France can still build a partnership of equals – based on respect rather than arrogance or domination.

rfi.title: Student-led movement seeks to unseat ruling party in Serbian election
rfi.description: Serbia's student-led protest movement is mounting its biggest challenge yet to former president Aleksandar Vucic, as voters prepare to elect a new parliament on Sunday after nearly two years of demonstrations against alleged corruption.

rfi.title: Orléans tightens security ahead of far-right National Rally party congress
rfi.description: Orléans says it will impose exceptional security measures ahead of the far-right National Rally's congress this weekend, when counter-demonstrations against "racism, fascism and imperialism" could drawn up to 25,000 people.

rfi.title: Casualties feared as multi-storey building collapses in Nairobi
rfi.description: A multi-storey building collapsed mid-construction in the Kenyan capital on Friday, with many feared trapped in the rubble and accusations of dangerous building work.

rfi.title: Kenya searches for missing Ugandan contact as Ebola cases rise

rfi.title: International Criminal Court wins EU's Sakharov human rights prize
rfi.description: Facing US sanctions, the International Criminal Court was on Thursday awarded the European Union's top rights prize, in a show of support that risks upsetting President Donald Trump.

rfi.title: Bill to make vandals pay for damage advances in wake of France's unrest
rfi.description: France has taken a further step towards making people financially responsible for damage they cause during urban riots in the wake of last weekend's unrest, when largely peaceful demonstrations over the cost of living were marred by widespread looting and destruction of public property.

rfi.title: Nearly all coral reefs at risk of collapse by 2075, conservation body warns
rfi.description: Nearly all of the world's shallow-water coral reefs face an extremely high risk of collapse within the next 50 years due to climate change, the International Union for Conservation of Nature, the the world's authority on endangered wildlife warned on Thursday.

lemonde.title: Au Brésil, les soutiens de Lula et de Bolsonaro mobilisés jusqu’au bout : « Mon père ne votait plus. Je l’ai convaincu que cette élection était la plus importante de notre vie »
lemonde.description: A la veille du scrutin présidentiel, le président de gauche, Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, candidat à un quatrième mandat, et son rival d’extrême droite, Flavio Bolsonaro, ont défilé avec leurs troupes pour tenter de convaincre les derniers indécis dans une course particulièrement serrée.

lemonde.title: Une journée de forte mobilisation sans incidents majeurs : « Le droit de manifester est aussi important que le droit de vote »
lemonde.description: Malgré des autorisations et des parcours souvent décidés à la dernière minute, près de 410 000 personnes – 800 000 selon la CGT – ont défilé dans le calme, samedi en France, contre la vie chère, en soutien aux lycéens ou pour les libertés publiques. Des heurts ont éclaté à Nantes, à Rennes et à Marseille en fin de journée, mais sans commune mesure avec les événements du 17 octobre.

lemonde.title: Attentat raciste de Trappes : le suspect transféré en soins psychiatriques ; son analyse de sang a révélé la présence de cannabis et de cocaïne
lemonde.description: Une observation en soins psychiatriques, qui suspend la mesure de garde à vue et peut durer quarante-huit heures, « doit permettre d’apprécier si son état de santé psychiatrique est compatible avec la possibilité de poursuivre ses auditions », a expliqué le Parquet national antiterroriste, dimanche matin.

lemonde.title: A Tel-Aviv, sur la « place des otages », la revanche des familles endeuillées du 7-Octobre
lemonde.description: Avant les élections législatives du mardi 27 octobre, des milliers d’Israéliens se sont rassemblés, samedi soir, en soutien aux familles d’otages qui réclament toujours une commission d’enquête d’Etat sur la tragédie. Gadi Eisenkot, grand rival du premier ministre sortant, y a fait une apparition triomphale.

lemonde.title: Midterms 2026 : pour les démocrates, la reconquête du Sénat passe par le Maine
lemonde.description: Tout ce que le parti compte de forces vives est venu soutenir Troy Jackson, candidat à la sénatoriale du 3 novembre. Situé à la gauche du parti, il défie la républicaine Susan Collins, élue sans discontinuer depuis trente ans dans cet Etat du Nord-Est américain.

lemonde.title: « Je n’ai pas la force de lutter contre l’IA » : face aux ravages de l’automatisation, une partie des jeunes se tourne vers des métiers manuels
lemonde.description: De jeunes actifs, dont la profession a été vidée de son sens par l’intelligence artificielle générative, décident de se reconvertir dans des secteurs préservés.

lemonde.title: A Orléans, une manifestation antifasciste empreinte de gravité et marquée par la division des gauches

lemonde.title: Avant le match de NFL au Stade de France, la tournée qui voulait introduire le football américain en France, en 1938
lemonde.description: Ce sport emblématique des Etats-Unis sera célébré dimanche 25 octobre dans l’enceinte de Seine-Saint-Denis. Déjà, à la veille de la seconde guerre mondiale, une équipe de vingt-quatre joueurs avait traversé l’Atlantique dans l’idée de l’importer dans le pays.

lemonde.title: La « fatigue informationnelle » touche de plus en plus de Français
lemonde.description: La troisième vague de l’enquête de L’Observatoire Société & Consommation et de la Fondation Jean Jaurès fait apparaître que 55 % des Français cherchent désormais à se protéger de l’information, en s’impliquant moins dans sa recherche et sa consultation. lemonde.title: « Les câbles sous-marins sont utilisés par la Russie ou la Chine pour affaiblir leurs ennemis et par les géants numériques pour asseoir leur domination »

france24fr.title: Attentat dans les Yvelines : garde à vue levée, le suspect placé en observation psychiatrique
france24fr.description: La garde à vue du suspect de l’attaque de Trappes a été levée et il a été placé en observation psychiatrique. Cette évaluation doit permettre de préciser son état de santé mentale et d’examiner une éventuelle dépendance aux stupéfiants, sans préjuger de sa responsabilité pénale. Le point sur la situation avec Gauthier Rybinski, chroniqueur international.

france24fr.title: Le Brésil aux urnes pour départager Lula et Bolsonaro, au coude-à-coude
france24fr.description: Quelque 160 millions d’électeurs sont appelés à désigner le prochain président du Brésil, alors que les bureaux de vote viennent d’ouvrir. Au coude-à-coude, Lula et Jair Bolsonaro incarnent deux orientations opposées pour le pays : la poursuite d’un pouvoir de gauche ou un retour à droite, dans un contexte de progression des droites proches de Donald Trump en Amérique latine. Notre correspondante Marine Resse décrit l’ambiance sur place.

france24fr.title: À Tel-Aviv, la gauche se mobilise contre Netanyahu à deux jours des législatives
france24fr.description: Un grand rassemblement de la gauche à Tel-Aviv s'est tenu samedi 24 octobre pour exprimer la volonté d’un changement politique à l’issue des élections législatives. À deux jours du vote, les manifestants affichent leur opposition à Benjamin Netanyahu, dans un scrutin perçu comme un référendum pour ou contre le Premier ministre. Récit d'Alice Brogat.

france24fr.title: Rwanda : le mystère autour de la mort de l'opposant Robert Kabera
france24fr.description: Les circonstances de la mort de Robert Kabera, ancien militaire rwandais réfugié en Ouganda et critique du gouvernement de Paul Kagame, restent entourées de nombreuses zones d'ombre. Sur sa chaîne YouTube, il publiait régulièrement des vidéos très critiques envers les autorités rwandaises et affirmait subir menaces et persécutions depuis son départ du pays. Human Rights Watch s'intéresse désormais à son cas. Correspondance d'Aurore Bayoud.

france24fr.title: Éthiopie : un forum consacré aux enjeux de sécurité en Afrique
france24fr.description: Anciens chefs d'État, attachés de défense et experts en sécurité se sont réunis dans la région Amhara, en Éthiopie, à l'occasion du Forum de Tana, consacré aux conflits armés et aux enjeux sécuritaires en Afrique. Une rencontre particulièrement importante pour Addis-Abeba, alors que le pays reste confronté à une rébellion armée et au risque d'une nouvelle crise régionale, que la médiation et le dialogue pourraient encore permettre d'éviter. Correspondance de Tom Canetti.

france24fr.title: Tchad : l'épidémie de dengue progresse et fait plusieurs dizaines de morts
france24fr.description: Depuis plusieurs semaines, le Tchad fait face à une épidémie de dengue, la deuxième seulement de son histoire. Plusieurs dizaines de personnes ont perdu la vie. La sécheresse et, plus largement, le changement climatique figurent parmi les facteurs favorisant la propagation du virus. Les autorités sanitaires ont lancé une vaste opération de pulvérisation pour tenter d'endiguer l'épidémie. Correspondance de Harold Girard au Tchad.

france24fr.title: Manifestations en France, frappes en Ukraine, présidentielle au Brésil : la semaine en images
france24fr.description: Retour sur les temps forts de l'actualité de la semaine écoulée et sur ses images les plus marquantes : les importantes dégradations en marge des manifestations nationales en France, les nouvelles frappes russes sur Kiev et les préparatifs pour les élections à venir au Brésil et en Israël.

france24fr.title: Mobilisation du 24 octobre : plus de 1 300 interpellations, une cinquantaine de policiers blessés
france24fr.description: Dimanche, le ministère de l’Intérieur a fait état de plus de 1 314 interpellations et de 53 membres des forces de l’ordre blessés, au lendemain de nouvelles manifestations en France. Au moins 410 000 personnes, selon les autorités, et 800 000 selon la CGT, avaient défilé.

france24fr.title: Attentat dans les Yvelines : le suspect placé en observation psychiatrique
france24fr.description: La garde à vue de l'homme soupçonné d'avoir tué une personne et blessé cinq autres dans les Yvelines a été levée pour raisons psychiatriques, a annoncé, dimanche, le parquet national antiterroriste. L'analyse toxicologique réalisée sur Kévin T. a révélé "la présence de cannabis et de cocaïne dans son sang", a par ailleurs indiqué le Pnat.

france24fr.title: Midterms : Trump va-t-il "tricher à tout va" ? Neuf scénarios possibles
france24fr.description: Donnés perdants aux prochaines élections de mi-mandat, les républicains et Donald Trump multiplient les initiatives controversées pour influencer le résultat. Son administration a déjà intenté un recours préventif en justice en cas de victoire démocrate en Alaska, ce qui fait craindre de futurs affrontements avec les États sur la validation des résultats. Voici les neuf scénarios jugés les plus probables par les experts.

france24fr.title: En France, la mobilisation du 24 octobre portée par les inquiétudes sur le pouvoir d’achat
france24fr.description: Entre 400 000 et 800 000 personnes ont manifesté samedi 24 octobre à travers la France. De Besançon à Strasbourg, en passant par Lille et Lyon, les cortèges ont placé le pouvoir d’achat au cœur des revendications, exprimant leurs inquiétudes face à la vie chère et leurs attentes pour améliorer le quotidien. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: À Orléans, Marine Le Pen lance sa campagne pour l’Élysée
france24fr.description: Marine Le Pen doit prononcer un grand discours de campagne en clôture du congrès du Rassemblement national, donnant le coup d’envoi officiel de sa course à l’Élysée. Autour du thème de la renaissance, elle entend insuffler de l’optimisme et mobiliser ses soutiens. Le point avec Elena Volochine, notre envoyée spéciale sur place.

france24fr.title: La NFL s'offre son premier match au Stade de France, Saints et Steelers visent les playoffs
france24fr.description: La France accueille pour la première fois, dimanche après-midi, un match de NFL, avec l'affiche entre les Saints de La Nouvelle-Orléans et les Steelers de Pittsburgh au Stade de France. À l'approche de la fin d'année, les deux équipes espèrent encore décrocher leur place en playoffs.

france24fr.title: "La hantise des éditeurs" : après l’affaire Thélyson Orélien, la chasse à l’IA s’organise
france24fr.description: L’affaire Thélyson Orélien, dont le roman "C’était ça ou mourir" est soupçonné d’avoir été écrit avec l’intelligence artificielle, secoue le monde de l’édition. Entre outils de détection, clauses contractuelles et création d’un label 100 % humain, les éditeurs organisent leur riposte tandis que les auteurs s’interrogent sur les conséquences pour la création.

france24fr.title: Israël bouclera la Cisjordanie occupée et fermera tous les points de passage lors des législatives
france24fr.description: L'armée israélienne a annoncé un bouclage de la Cisjordanie occupée mardi, jour des élections législatives en Israël. Cette mesure intervient alors que l'État hébreu mène une vaste opération dans ce territoire palestinien occupé et que 2 000 habitants d'Hébron ont été chassés de leurs foyers.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle au Brésil : Lula ou Bolsonaro, un choix décisif pour l'avenir du pays
france24fr.description: Quelque 160 millions d'électeurs sont appelés aux urnes, dimanche, au Brésil, pour départager le président de gauche Lula et le sénateur Flavio Bolsonaro, fils de l'ancien chef d'État d'extrême droite. Un scrutin décisif qui dira si le pays reste à gauche ou rejoint la vague conservatrice qui progresse en Amérique latine, encouragée par Donald Trump.

france24fr.title: En Serbie, des législatives sur fond de rejet du président Aleksandar Vucic
france24fr.description: Les Serbes sont appelés aux urnes, dimanche, pour des législatives anticipées, réclamées par un puissant mouvement étudiant qui présente une liste face au président Aleksandar Vucic. Les manifestants espèrent faire de ce scrutin un "référendum anti-Vucic", deux ans après la mort de 16 personnes dans l’effondrement d’un auvent à Novi Sad en 2024.

france24fr.title: Ultra-trail : l'incroyable exploit d'Hugo Deck à la Diagonale des Fous
france24fr.description: Avec les 180 km et 10.200 m de dénivelé positif de ce tracé, du sud au nord de l'île, à travers des pitons escarpés, des rivières et des forêts luxuriantes, la Diagonale des Fous est considérée comme l'une des courses en montagne les plus dures du monde. À 26 ans, et pour sa première participation, le Français Hugo Deck s'est imposé en seulement 22 h 54'19'', signant un nouveau record. Il nous raconte les coulisses de son exploit.

zeit.description: Die meisten Blaubeeren kommen heute aus Peru. Wie wachsen sie dort? Wer pflückt sie? Was steckt hinter den Gesundheitsversprechen? Wir sind der Frucht hinterhergereist

zeit.title: Anthony Sintow-Behrens: »Man spielt mit dem Kopf Klavier und lernt, den Körper zu benutzen«
zeit.description: Anthony Sintow-Behrens, 25, hat das Fußballspielen für seine Karriere aufgegeben. Er sagt: Selbst Bowling ist für seine Hände gefährlich.

zeit.title: Flaggenquiz: 197 Flaggen, los geht’s!
zeit.description: Um dieses Quiz zu meistern, müssen Sie Flaggen aus der ganzen Welt erkennen. Nichts einfacher als das? Gut, denn wir zeigen Ihnen nur die Farbanteile.

zeit.title: Auswanderung von Jüdinnen: Wo ist noch Heimat?
zeit.description: Sie sind beide Jüdinnen. Die eine hält es in Israel nicht mehr aus und geht mit ihrer Familie nach Deutschland. Die andere flieht aus den Niederlanden – nach Israel.

zeit.title: Wohnungskrise: Alexander Dobrindt legt Eckpunkte für Investitionsschutzgesetz vor
zeit.description: Die Bundesregierung will mit Blick auf die Berliner Regierungsbildung Vergesellschaftungen erschweren. Laut einem Entwurf sollen Entschädigungen sofort fällig werden.

zeit.title: Herbstwetter: Wetterdienst erwartet Temperaturen von über 20 Grad
zeit.description: Nach dem stürmischen Wochenende sagen Meteorologen vor allem im Süden Deutschlands milde Herbsttage voraus. Im Norden bleibt es wechselhaft.

nzz.title: VIDEO - Deutsch-israelische Politikberaterin über die Lage in Israel
nzz.description: Melody Sucharewicz ist deutsch-israelische Politikberaterin und Expertin für Extremismusbekämpfung. NZZ-Chefredaktor Eric Gujer spricht mit ihr über Israels Lage, die Stimmung im Land und die Prognosen für die anstehenden Wahlen.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Ebola-Ausbruch in Zentralafrika: Uganda verschärft Einreisemassnahmen
nzz.description: Die Weltgesundheitsorganisation (WHO) hat den Gesundheitsnotstand ausgerufen. Die Infektionszahlen steigen weiterhin an. Hier sind die wichtigsten Antworten zum Ebola-Virus zu finden.

nzz.title: Weniger Plünderungen, aber erneut Gewalt bei den Protesten in Frankreich – auch in Italien kommt es zu Schäden und Angriffen
nzz.description: Lange verliefen die Proteste in Frankreich am Samstag friedlich. Doch am Rand der Demonstrationen griffen Gewalttätige wieder die Polizei an. Heftig krachte es in Tours.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN WIRTSCHAFT - Migros plant grundlegenden Konzernumbau
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus der Wirtschaft.

nzz.title: «Keine Hängematte mehr»: Österreich kürzt Sozialhilfe für Grossfamilien und verschärft Regeln für Migranten
nzz.description: Wer die vollen Sozialleistungen beziehen will, muss künftig Integrationsbemühungen nachweisen. Die Regierung will das System so für Zuwanderer unattraktiver machen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Iran greift Stellung im Irak an
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Frankreichs Innenminister spricht von mehr als 1000 Festnahmen
nzz.description: Seit Ende September gehen Schüler, Lehrpersonen und Gewerkschaften auf die Strasse – und lösen eine landesweite Bewegung aus, die zu Krawallen und Gewalt führt. Die neusten Entwicklungen.

nzz.title: Hitlers «Teehaus» am Obersalzberg brennt nieder: Der mutmassliche Brandstifter ist laut der Staatsanwaltschaft psychisch krank
nzz.description: Die Berggaststätte Kehlsteinhaus hoch über Berchtesgaden ging in der Nacht auf Samstag in Flammen auf. Die Polizei hat eine verdächtige Person festgenommen. Die Ruine soll wieder aufgebaut werden.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Starlink läuft laut Selenski wieder
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Die ukrainische Armee verlegt den Bewegungskrieg in den Untergrund
nzz.description: Soldaten des Chartia-Korps kämpfen sich bei Kupjansk erfolgreich durch eine Gasleitung hinter die russischen Linien durch. Die Erfolgsmeldung stützt das militärische Selbstbewusstsein der Ukraine in einem kritischen Moment.

nzz.title: Von Trump bis Milei: Wer den Bolsonaros nahesteht
nzz.description: Flávio Bolsonaro fordert in der Stichwahl Präsident Lula heraus. Der Bolsonaro-Clan hat sich ein Netzwerk aufgebaut, das weit über Brasilien hinausreicht.

nzz.title: Bürgerlich, nichtbinär, Berufsaktivist: Benjamin Ball gehört zu den Organisatoren der Protestwelle in Frankreich
nzz.description: Der 42-jährige Franzose ist einer von sieben Koordinatoren der Gelbwesten, doch er tritt nun besonders in Erscheinung. Die Gewalt bei den Protesten findet er legitim. Wir haben mit ihm gesprochen.

nzz.title: Europas Jugend probt den Aufstand: Der Gen-Z-Sozialismus erobert die Strasse
nzz.description: Preiskontrollen, Enteignungen von Wohnbauunternehmen und Gratisdienste der öffentlichen Hand: Von Paris bis Berlin verlangen die Jungen, dass der Staat sie vor der Welt schützt. So viel anders als bei den Rechtspopulisten ist das nicht.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - PHP-Panne: «Manche werden auch nach dem hundertsten Weckruf nicht wach», sagt ein Experte für Cybersicherheit
nzz.description: Manuel Atug sieht Hacker im KI-Zeitalter im Vorteil. Und er fordert: Die Verantwortung für Cybersicherheit in Firmen und Behörden müsse eingehalten werden – auf höchster Führungsebene.

nzz.title: Ein Anlageplan für unruhige Zeiten
nzz.description: Wieso Investoren derzeit nicht nur auf Mainstream-Anlagen setzen sollten.

spiegel.title: Florian Schroeder: Neue ZDF-Sendung »Journal Deluxe« sorgt für Debatte
spiegel.description: Witze über Linke und Grüne. Und Alice Weidel als Gast? Mit seiner neuen ZDF-Sendung »Journal Deluxe« provoziert Florian Schroeder schon vor der Premiere. Hier sagt er, ob das Kalkül war.

spiegel.title: Cartoons der Woche: Friedrich Merz in der Krise, Debatte über Rot-Grün-Rot in Berlin
spiegel.description: Horrorszenario Rot-Grün-Rot – gehen Politiker in Berlin bald auf die Barrikaden? Kanzler Merz im Gruselkabinett. Und: Staatsverschuldung zum Fürchten. Sehen Sie hier die Cartoons der Woche.

spiegel.title: Neapel: Deutscher Tourist will Kokain kaufen – und bekommt Speisesalz
spiegel.description: Der vermeintliche Dealer kassierte 40 Euro, der Käufer bekam Kochsalz: In Italien ist ein deutscher Tourist auf einen angeblichen Kokainverkäufer hereingefallen. Carabinieri in Zivil hielten beide an.

spiegel.title: Sylvester Stallone: Warum der Schauspieler Nepotismus für sinnvoll hält
spiegel.description: Der Hollywoodschauspieler wurde von seinen Eltern nicht unterstützt. Mit seiner eigenen Tochter will er offenbar anders umgehen – auch wenn es nach außen unfair wirkt.

spiegel.title: Katholische Kirche: Erzdiözese New York zahlt Opfern von Missbrauch mehr als 800 Millionen Dollar
spiegel.description: 1300 Menschen hatten Geistlichen innerhalb des Erzbistums New York sexuellen Missbrauch vorgeworfen. Nun haben sich Kirche und Opfer auf einen Vergleich geeinigt. Auch Dokumente über ‌die Täter sollen zugänglich werden.

spiegel.title: FC Barcelona gegen Real Madrid: José Mourinho spielt seine bekannten Hits
spiegel.description: Trainer-Altmeister José Mourinho steht mit Real Madrid beim Clásico in Barcelona unter Druck – und reagiert darauf wie gewohnt: Er nimmt die Schiedsrichter ins Visier.

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag
spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

spiegel.title: SC Freiburg gegen FC Bayern München: Matthias Ginter über das badische Erfolgsrezept
spiegel.description: Wenig Geld, großer Erfolg: Seit Jahren spielt der SC Freiburg stärker, als es die Clubfinanzen eigentlich hergeben. Nun trifft der Verein auf die Bayern – zum Spitzenspiel. Ex-Nationalspieler Matthias Ginter über das badische Geheimnis.

spiegel.title: Formel 1: Kimi Antonelli startete von der Pole Position beim Großen Preis der USA in Austin
spiegel.description: Es war eine deutliche Ansage an die Konkurrenz: Kimi Antonelli hat das Qualifying beim Großen Preis der USA in Austin für sich entschieden. Schon am Abend kann er sich zum neuen Weltmeister küren.

spiegel.title: Emmanuel Macron: So wurde der Präsident zum Buhmann der Protestjugend
spiegel.description: Was als Aufstand gegen die Zustände an Schulen begann, ist zu einer breiten Front gegen den scheidenden Präsidenten geworden. Der Frust der Franzosen auf Emmanuel Macron ist vor allem für die politische Mitte gefährlich.

spiegel.title: Sturm-Warnung für Teile Deutschlands, Sturmflut-Gefahr an der Nordseeküste
spiegel.description: Teils heftiger Wind sorgt für einen ungemütlichen Wochenausklang. Der Wetterdienst warnt vor teils schweren Sturmböen. An der Nordseeküste kann es zu einer Sturmflut kommen.

spiegel.title: Smartphone-Nutzung: Der Esstisch gilt vielen als digitale Tabuzone
spiegel.description: »Jetzt guckt der schon wieder auf sein Handy …« Solche Gedanken haben im Digitalzeitalter Konjunktur. Eine Umfrage zeigt, wann der Blick aufs Handy besonders stört.

spiegel.title: Schlaf: Haben Menschen früher besser geschlafen als wir heute?
spiegel.description: Die Zeitumstellung bereitet vielen Menschen Probleme mit dem Schlaf. Entspannung bringen könnte ein Blick in die Vergangenheit, meint ein US-Historiker. Damals hätten die Menschen gar nicht den Anspruch gehabt, durchzuschlafen.

spiegel.title: Elektroauto kaufen: Hohe Spritpreise treiben Nachfrage nach E-Autos an
spiegel.description: Die anhaltend hohen Spritpreise haben die Nachfrage nach Elektroautos angekurbelt. Die negative Begleiterscheinung: Die Verkäufer geizen zunehmend mit Rabatten.

spiegel.title: News: Die CDU und ihre vier strategischen Probleme
spiegel.description: Warum die einst stolze Volkspartei dem Untergang entgegentaumelt. Das ist die Lage am Sonntag.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Mindestens 1000 Festnahmen bei Protesten gegen soziale Ungerechtigkeit
spiegel.description: Das zweite Protestwochenende in Frankreich ist wesentlich friedlicher verlaufen. In den Großstädten kam es aber doch zu Zusammenstößen zwischen Demonstranten und Polizei. Und zahlreichen Festnahmen.

spiegel.title: Thomas Markle: Herzogin Meghan brach wegen Vorwürfen Kontakt per Brief ab
spiegel.description: Eine philippinische Taskforce soll das frühere Wohnhaus von Thomas Markle durchsucht und Darstellungen sexuellen Missbrauchs von Kindern sichergestellt haben. Herzogin Meghan konfrontierte ihren Vater Berichten zufolge bereits 2025 mit den Vorwürfen.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: Andy Burnham offen für Rückkehr zu EU-Freizügigkeit
spiegel.description: Mit dem Brexit begann für die Wirtschaft eine schwere Zeit im Handel mit Großbritannien. Als massives Beschwernis erwies sich das Ende der offenen Grenzen. Jetzt sendet Premier Andy Burnham überraschende Signale.

letemps.description:
Maud * et Rubyna, deux jeunes femmes atteintes de cette maladie chronique auto-immune, témoignent d’un quotidien fait de crises inopinées et de séquelles variables. Des chercheurs bâlois ouvrent la voie à une meilleure prédiction de la progression de cette pathologie

Pour ses 50 ans, les Editions Phébus font reparaître un ovni de la littérature. Ecrit dans les années 1930, publié une première fois en 1941, «La Boîte en os», d’Antoinette Peské, est un bijou gothique que n’aurait pas renié Edgar Allan Poe

letemps.description:
Ernst Tanner revient dans une interview accordée à NZZ am Sonntag sur la rupture inédite que traverse le chocolatier zurichois depuis plusieurs mois. Il ne voit pas de raison urgente de se retirer de la tête du conseil d’administration, malgré ses 80 ans

letemps.description:
Hyper-contrôle, effondrement, apocalypse: nos imaginaires sont saturés de futurs catastrophiques qui affectent majoritairement les jeunes. Face à l’angoisse, de nouveaux récits défendent l’espoir. L’écologue Anne-Caroline Prévot analyse la manière dont la fiction peut modifier notre rapport à la nature

letemps.title: Pour l’industrie suisse de la défense, le cadre légal actuel n’offre que deux choix: délocaliser ou fermer

phys-org.description: The most comprehensive record yet of carbon dioxide stored underground through geological carbon dioxide storage has been published today, revealing that 43.6 million metric tons were sequestered in 2024 alone—a new annual record—and that 421.7 million metric tons have now been stored in the past three decades.

phys-org.title: Sea cucumber–inspired gel could help heal damaged tissue in humans
phys-org.description: Inspired by the ability of sea cucumbers to change the stiffness of their bodies, University of Waterloo researchers have developed a gel that could one day help repair damaged tendons and other soft tissues without leaving permanent material behind.

phys-org.title: Who should have a say in which species are saved? The California condor offers lessons for a global biodiversity treaty
phys-org.description: In 1987, biologists captured the last free-flying condor to transfer it to captivity, and the largest flying North American bird species was officially declared extinct in the wild. Today, after decades of coordinated efforts and millions of dollars spent on captive breeding and reintroduction efforts, more than 300 condors have been restored to their natural environment.

phys-org.title: Bell pepper colors reveal differences in sweetness, nutrients and ripeness
phys-org.description: Raw, grilled, roasted, stuffed—there are many ways to enjoy bell peppers, also called capsicums, sweet peppers or paprika. Bell peppers originated in Central and South America and belong to the nightshade family along with tomatoes and eggplants.

phys-org.title: Tests reveal why titanium additions do not fully prevent pitting corrosion in stainless steel
phys-org.description: Stainless steel is widely used for its corrosion resistance, but it is not invincible. In environments containing chloride ions, such as seawater, pitting corrosion can occur. These pits often start at tiny particles called inclusions embedded in the steel.

phys-org.title: Single X-ray pulse reveals plasma nanostructures across scales with one camera
phys-org.description: Understanding instabilities and turbulence in plasmas is one of the key challenges across a wide range of plasma research fields, including nuclear fusion, astrophysics and laser-plasma physics. In plasmas, slight disturbances can grow due to instabilities, and energy is transferred between structures of various sizes due to turbulence. These phenomena give rise to structures ranging from very small to large, which significantly influence the overall motion and energy flow of the plasma.

phys-org.title: How flare ribbons reveal hidden solar explosions on the sun
phys-org.description: Many topics in astronomy and astrophysics are esoteric. There's not much of a relationship between something like the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way and the life of a regular person going about their business. But the sun is different. Its presence in our lives is inescapable. Its behavior, especially its flaring, has an impact.

phys-org.title: 'One-positron cyclotron' could test a key prediction of the Standard Model
phys-org.description: The positron is the antimatter counterpart of the electron, identical in mass but carrying an equal and opposite electric charge. Like the electron, it also behaves like a tiny bar magnet, and according to a key prediction of the Standard Model of particle physics, its magnetic moment should be exactly equal and opposite to the electron's.

phys-org.title: Newly identified protein pathway helps HIV stay hidden despite treatment
phys-org.description: Current HIV medicines are effective at suppressing the virus in the blood. However, HIV can remain "asleep" or dormant inside certain immune cells and in the brain. These hidden pockets of virus, called HIV reservoirs, are the main reason HIV cannot be cured with today's treatments.

phys-org.title: Nanoscale alloy redesign tackles cold brittleness for potential deep-space and deep-sea applications
phys-org.description: Metallic materials used in extremely cold environments must maintain high strength, ductility and fracture toughness to support applications in aerospace, clean energy, superconducting systems and deep-space exploration. However, traditional alloys often suffer performance degradation at ultralow temperatures because of the long-standing trade-off between strength, ductility and toughness. Although metals may become stronger at lower temperatures, they can also become more brittle and prone to f

phys-org.title: Seabird family tree predicts which species accumulate plastic better than diet, global analysis finds
phys-org.description: What seabirds eat might seem like a good starting point for identifying species that tend to accumulate plastic in their digestive systems. Yet a recent global analysis suggests that mapping the evolutionary relatives of birds could offer better clues than their diets or feeding methods alone.

phys-org.title: Ancient stalagmites reveal exceptions to Asia–South America monsoon seesaw over the past 450,000 years
phys-org.description: In places like South Asia, Africa and parts of the Americas, monsoon rains supply water for drinking, crops and hydropower for billions of people. Understanding the patterns that monsoons tend to follow can help people plan for drought risks affecting agriculture, reservoirs and hydropower across distant regions.

phys-org.title: Cleaner brick kilns cut pollution, but gains did not reach workers, research finds

phys-org.title: Surveying the genetic battlefield to uncover the rules of rapid evolution
phys-org.description: The Malik Lab thrives on competition. But for HHMI investigator Harmit Malik and his team at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, it's the genomes—not the people—that are in conflict. The lab studies rapid evolution—the genetic changes that happen in a species over a few generations rather than thousands of years. These fast changes are often fueled by genetic conflicts—competitions between different entities trying to maximize their success at the expense of another.

undark.title: Podcast: The Entanglements Series Finale

undark.title: Podcast: Is There a Population Crisis?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Michael Geruso, an associate professor of economics at the University of Texas at Austin, and Jennifer Dowd, a professor of demography and population health at the University of Oxford, about population trends and fertility rates.

undark.title: Podcast: Which Animals Are Conscious?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Heather Browning, a philosopher at the University of Southampton in the U.K, and Deb Brown, a philosopher and the  director of the Critical Thinking Project at the University of Queensland in Australia, about which animals feel pain and more.

undark.title: Podcast: Is ADHD Actually a Disorder?

undark.title: Podcast: Should We Put AI-Enabled Tech in Our Brains?
undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

public-dom.description: In the late nineteenth century, visitors to Maine observed something strange: French-Canadian lumberjacks who, at the slightest stimulus, seemed to jump, strike out with their limbs, or mimic languages they could not speak. Ross Bullen introduces us to these so-called “Jumping Frenchmen” and to their greatest investigator, George M. Beard, who saw a link in their behavior between religious frenzy and neurasthenia.

public-dom.title: Philip Sidney and the Extreme (Dis)graces of the Parenthesis
public-dom.description: Erasmus called them “little moons” and George Puttenham praised them as “figures of tolerable disorder” (if used not too often “nor too thick”). For Philip Sidney, they were simply indispensable. Florence Hazrat introduces us to the uncontested early modern king of brackets and to his romance Arcadia, which abruptly ends, like its author’s life, hanging on a parenthesis.

public-dom.title: “There is Nothing but Immortality!”: Walt Whitman and The Book of Heavenly Death (1905)
public-dom.description: Choice excerpts from *Leaves of Grass* that speak to Whitman’s conception of immortality.

public-dom.title: Anatomy Unzipped: John of Arderne’s Sweden Scroll (ca. 1425–35)
public-dom.description: Early surgical diagrams that present patients prying themselves open for our anatomical gaze.

public-dom.title: In Company Style: Illustrations from James Skinner’s Kitāb-i tashrīḥ al-aqvām (1825)
public-dom.description: An illuminated Persian manuscript about customs, culture, and caste, written by an enigmatic figure of the early British Raj.

public-dom.title: Veronese's Dogs
public-dom.description: “Oh, if I could only pray”, Luther once said of his dog Tölpel, “the way this dog watches the meat”. Attending to attentive canine figures in half a dozen paintings by Paolo Veronese, Thomas W. Laqueur explores the work of an artist whose love of dogs landed him in hot water with the Inquisition.

public-dom.title: It’s “A Cat-astrophe”! (1919)
public-dom.description: “A Cat-astrophe” came on the tail end of an odd 1918 boom in cat-themed music.

public-dom.title: Metamorphosis: Transformations in the Early Modern Flap Book (early 19th century)
public-dom.description: By manipulating paper flaps, the child could turn Adam into Eve into a mermaid, a lion into a griffin into an eagle — all while learning about the inevitability of death.

public-dom.title: The Ties that Bind: Central Asian Ikat (ca. 19th century)
public-dom.description: Vibrant textiles from the dazzling Timurid metropolis of Bukhara.

public-dom.title: Artificial Intelligence: Ars Notoria and the Promise of Instant Knowledge
public-dom.description: Centuries before Neo instantly mastered Kung Fu in *The Matrix*, medieval scholars found a shortcut to years of difficult study: a magical manuscript that promised to fast-track advanced learning. Anne Lawrence-Mathers investigates the *Ars notoria*, its supposed powers, and the demonic influence it had upon some users.

public-dom.title: Photographs of Atlantic City Sand Sculpture (ca. 1880–1920)
public-dom.description: Photographs from when Atlantic City beaches featured artists ornately sculpting sand.

public-dom.title: “The Persian Mâr-Nâmeh or, The Book for Taking Omens from Snakes” (1892)
public-dom.description: A Zoroastrian text about serpents translated by the President of the Bombay Anthropological Society.

proj-syn.description: If current trends continue, the Chinese state will find itself exposed to a political succession crisis, a weakening economy, and a lack of resources to exercise power domestically and project it externally. It would be a perfect storm, with far-reaching global repercussions.

While Europe has much to do to improve its external competitiveness, it must not ac

proj-syn.title: Who Pays the Fiscal Watchdogs?
proj-syn.description: Civil-society oversight is the cheapest insurance in sovereign finance, because it enables independent scrutiny long before a default. But given that a borrowing government will never volunteer to fund the people who audit it, global decision-makers must do so using agreements for stolen-asset recovery and sovereign-debt treatments.

proj-syn.title: How to Help Left-Behind Regions
proj-syn.description: Pouring public investment into poorer towns and cities might be politically beneficial, but the economic returns of indiscriminate largesse would be limited. A better approach would concentrate investment in areas with the potential to become high-productivity hubs, such as large peripheral cities.

proj-syn.title: The Agentic Information Economy
proj-syn.description: An internet populated and run by AI agents will need not just reliable data but also a broader information ecology capable of questioning its own inputs and transmitting corrections where they are needed if information changes. But whether this will serve private interests or the public good remains to be seen.

proj-syn.title: A Competitive Europe Must Be Climate-Resilient
proj-syn.description: Extreme weather and climate-related events caused €822 billion in economic losses across the European Union between 1980 and 2024, with a quarter of the losses occurring just in the last five years. The consequences for Europe’s competitiveness and economic security are clear—and so is the appropriate response.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Prepare for the Worst
proj-syn.description: Those seeking to weaken the EU’s supranational foundations are already preparing their radical schemes, like the “new deal for Europe” that Germany's Alternative für Deutschland recently presented in the European Parliament. The pro-EU camp must be prepared with new political strategies and institutional arrangements.

proj-syn.title: Nature Can’t Wait
proj-syn.description: Although the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine are spurring governments to increase spending on defense and focus more on economic growth, it would be a mistake to postpone investments designed to protect nature. In fact, meeting internationally agreed targets could add up to $450 billion to annual global GDP by 2050.

proj-syn.title: Argentina’s Economic Chainsaw Massacre
proj-syn.description: Argentine President Javier Milei may currently be a lynchpin in US President Donald Trump’s geoeconomic vision for Latin America; but he could soon become its weak link. With elections coming next year, he has achieved an economic recovery and relative price stability by driving millions of his people into destitution.

proj-syn.title: Which AI Myth Will We Embrace?
proj-syn.description: The mythos—or foundational stories—that we tell ourselves will determine our fate in the age of AI. As industry leaders regale us with utopian visions of benevolent digital gods delivering scientific breakthroughs and expanding our technological horizons, our best defense against hubris is a counternarrative of social cooperation.

proj-syn.title: No More Superpowers
proj-syn.description: Although the United States remains very powerful and Russia still commands enormous conventional and nuclear capabilities, each country’s global status has come to be defined by failure and constraint. If anything, both may belong to the same broad grouping of middle powers that includes the likes of Canada, Brazil, and India.

proj-syn.title: What’s Driving Persistent Inflation?
proj-syn.description: In their preoccupation with high public debt, rising bond yields, and dizzying AI valuations, investors have seemingly forgotten the supply shocks shaping the underlying inflation outlook. But anyone worried about debt and yields must reckon with the disruptions created in the name of protecting domestic markets.

proj-syn.title: Building the Economy Africa Needs
proj-syn.description: Africa cannot control global geopolitics, let alone prevent external shocks. But it can manage its exposure, especially by building an integrated continental market, investing in higher-value-added production, and pushing for reform of the global credit-rating agencies.

proj-syn.title: Science Without Scientists?
proj-syn.description: Now that autonomous systems are capable of generating their own hypotheses, designing experiments, and writing up the results, the scientific community must adapt. For scientific knowledge to retain its standing, its sources must be trusted and answerable to the public.

proj-syn.title: When Smart Cities Turn Menacing
proj-syn.description: Uganda has embraced digital-surveillance tools in the name of improving public safety and combating terrorism, a pattern that is repeating itself across several African countries. But governments are increasingly using these technologies for political control, rather than for national security.

proj-syn.title: Brazil Cannot Afford Bolsonaro’s Spending Cuts
proj-syn.description: If he wins the October 25 runoff, far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro plans to slash public spending by as much as 1.5% of GDP. These cuts could push Brazil into recession, hurt workers and small businesses, and drain tax revenue—all without solving the country’s debt problem.

proj-syn.title: A Generational Reckoning on the Streets of Paris
proj-syn.description: As their schools deteriorate and the planet grows hotter, many young people in France do not have hope for a decent future. The recent protests may foreshadow a broader conflict between older generations who wield political power and younger people who must live in the world they leave behind.

proj-syn.title: The Algorithm Driving French Student Protests
proj-syn.description: One of the main drivers of the student protests in France is the opposition to Parcoursup, the country’s university-admissions platform, which is widely denounced as opaque and unfair. While such automated decision-making systems do not create educational inequalities, they can exacerbate them.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI Drives A Varied Lineup Of Large Financings
crunchbase.description: It was another interesting week for AI-related startup funding, with a number of large rounds and quirky companies. The largest financings went to Tenstorrent, a developer of AI processors and systems, and AI lab Flapping Airplanes. The quirkiest round, meanwhile, was undoubtedly a $200 million financing for Warhound, which wants to breed elite military dogs. A number of big rounds in areas including biotech, space tech and physical AI rounded out the list.

crunchbase.title: Protecting Trade Secrets In The Age Of AI
crunchbase.description: AI agents create new trade secret risks by allowing employees to access expertise or inadvertently expose proprietary information through personal devices. In this guest commentary, Seth Kugler, a partner at Grellas Shah LLP, warns companies that they should adopt strict AI policies, restrict data access on unmanaged devices, update confidentiality agreements, and act immediately when misuse is suspected.

crunchbase.title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: Robot Training, Space Lasers And Greener Cement
crunchbase.description: From teaching robots to do everyday household chores to using lasers to track satellites in space, this month's crop of interesting startup deals spans some decidedly different corners of tech.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: Slingshot Raises $27M In Seed Funding To Build An Insurer For Those Small Policies Sold At Checkout
crunchbase.description: Slingshot Insurance, a Minneapolis-based AI-native embedded insurance startup, is emerging from stealth with $27 million in a seed funding round co-led by Rally Ventures and Skyward Group, it tells Crunchbase News exclusively.

crunchbase.title: The AI IPO Wave Is The Dot-Com Bubble’s Evil Twin. Anthropic’s Delay Just Proved It.
crunchbase.description: In this guest article from Airrived co-founder and CEO Anurag Gurtu, he contends that Anthropic’s rapid revenue growth does not justify its proposed $2 trillion IPO valuation, given enormous infrastructure commitments, safety concerns, customer concentration and competition from cheaper open-weight models, saying instead that lasting enterprise AI value will come from proprietary data, reliable deployment and measurable customer outcomes rather than expensive models alone.

crunchbase.title: Acquirers Are Snapping Up Boom-Era Startups That Haven’t Raised Funding In Years
crunchbase.description: A number of companies whose names might feature on a playlist of 2021 boom-era unicorns have sold to acquirers in recent months, including one-time highfliers like Airtable, Headspace and Miro. In many cases, companies are selling at valuations which, while not puny, are still far below their former peaks.

crunchbase.title: Your Next Customer Might Be An Agent. Here’s How To Build Your Brand For Both Humans And AI.
crunchbase.description: As AI agents increasingly recommend and purchase products, brands must appeal to both machines and humans by documenting their voice, creating clear product descriptions and checking how AI summarizes their messaging. Guest author Toby Coulthard suggests that startups should build these practices in from the outset, preserving human appeal while measuring success through conversions and revenue rather than content volume.

crunchbase.title: When A Startup Sells, Its Employees’ Equity Plans Can Change Overnight
crunchbase.description: Startup acquisitions can reshape employees’ finances and careers, with individual outcomes depending on a variety of conditions. Guest author Ron Honig, co-CEO and managing partner of From-Honig Family Office, suggests that before making major life changes, employees should clarify their award rights, when proceeds will become available, and what their after-tax payout can realistically support.

crunchbase.title: ‘Weird And Maybe Uninvestable’: How Reach Capital Spots Its Venture Winners
crunchbase.description: Crunchbase News spoke with James Kim, partner at Reach Capital, about how Reach’s education roots inform its broader strategy, what it saw in AI detection company GPTZero, and why some of its best investments initially divided its own team. We also discussed how ownership stakes and secondary transactions have shaped the firm’s approach to returning capital.

crunchbase.title: How To Build A Billion-Dollar Company Without Venture Capital
crunchbase.description: Founders can build billion-dollar businesses without venture capital by prioritizing customer revenue, pricing for quality, hiring exceptional talent and automating processes to scale efficiently, argues Nacho De Marco, who draws on his experience bootstrapping BairesDev, to emphasize financial discipline and a lasting commitment to solving customer problems as the foundations of sustainable growth.
